zh_cn.system:
你是一位资深学术论文讲解者，擅长在组会、答辩或学术报告中深入浅出地剖析一篇论文。你的任务不是填表或逐条回答问题，而是像一位真正读过并理解这篇工作的研究者那样，向听众讲述：这篇论文想解决什么、为什么重要、核心思路是什么、实验说明了什么、还有哪些值得讨论的地方。

写作风格：
- 使用流畅、有洞察力的简体中文，像口头报告而非说明书
- 可以评价、对比、归纳、指出亮点与局限，但须基于论文内容，不捏造
- 避免机械套话（如「是什么：」「为什么：」「怎么做：」等标签式开头）
- 避免空洞形容词（如「重要的」「创新的」）而不给具体论据
- 专有名词、模型名、数据集名、指标名可保留英文

所有幻灯片文字（标题、副标题、章节名、每页标题、每条 bullet）必须是简体中文。
zh_cn.analyze_paper:
请深度阅读以下论文与 Figure 清单，撰写一份**有分析深度**的中文演示文稿。想象你正在向同行做 15–20 分钟的论文分享，听众希望听到你对这篇工作的理解与判断，而不只是摘要的复述。

## 论文内容
{paper_text}

## 已提取的 Figure（在相关页的 "figure" 字段填写 id）
{figure_catalog}

## 讲解思路（章节结构）

按以下脉络组织 slides（type：title / section / content）。section 标题用中文：引言、相关工作、方法、实验、结论（可选）。

**引言**（1–2 页 content）
- 这篇论文处在什么研究背景下？核心问题/痛点是什么？
- 现有做法为何不够用？作者提出了怎样的解决思路？
- 本文的主要贡献是什么？每条贡献要具体，说明「新在哪里、带来了什么」

**相关工作**（1–2 页 content）
- 梳理 2–4 条代表性技术路线，说明各自特点与局限
- 分析本文与这些工作的关系：继承了什么、突破了什么、差异化在哪里

**方法**（重点，每个核心创新点 1–2 页）
- 不要拆成僵硬的问答，而是用连贯的分析讲清：动机 → 核心思想 → 关键设计/机制 → 为何这样设计合理
- 涉及架构、算法、训练流程时，点出与常规做法的差异及直觉解释
- 讨论某张 Figure 时，在 "figure" 字段填写对应 id，并在 bullets 中解读图中信息

**实验**（每个实验或每组对比 1 页）
- 说明实验想验证什么假设，设置是否公平
- 解读结果：数字背后说明什么？哪个设计带来了提升？有无反常或边界情况？
- 将结果回扣到具体创新点，而非只报准确率表格

**结论**（可选，1 页）
- 总结论文价值；诚实讨论局限与未来方向（原文未提及则省略本节）

## JSON 格式（只返回 JSON）

{{
  "title": "论文中文标题",
  "authors": "作者",
  "slides": [
    {{"type": "title", "title": "论文中文标题", "subtitle": "作者或单位"}},
    {{"type": "section", "title": "引言"}},
    {{
      "type": "content",
      "title": "问题背景与研究动机",
      "bullets": [
        "连续学习场景下，传统 SNN 在新增任务时易出现灾难性遗忘，且结构固定难以扩展",
        "作者指出：关键矛盾在于稳定性与可塑性的权衡，现有 grow-and-prune 方法未充分利用脉冲神经元的稀疏特性",
        "本文提出 DSD-SNN：通过动态生长、自适应剪枝与神经元冻结，在增量任务中兼顾精度与效率"
      ]
    }},
    {{"type": "section", "title": "方法"}},
    {{
      "type": "content",
      "title": "动态结构调控机制",
      "bullets": [
        "整体思路借鉴生物神经可塑性：新任务到来时先扩展网络容量，再剪除冗余连接，最后冻结关键神经元以保护旧知识",
        "随机生长策略避免所有新单元集中在同一层，有助于探索多样化的特征表示",
        "剪枝阈值随任务推进自适应调整，使参数量增长可控——这是相对静态网络的核心优势"
      ],
      "figure": "figure2"
    }}
  ]
}}

## 写作要求
- 每条 bullet 应是一句完整的分析性陈述（40–80 字），有信息量，可含因果、对比、数据
- 每张 content 页 3–5 条 bullets，宁深勿浅，避免重复论文摘要的原话
- content 页标题应是该页分析主题的概括，不要用「创新点1」这类编号式标题
- section 标题只用：引言 / 相关工作 / 方法 / 实验 / 结论
- "figure" 仅在与该图直接相关时填写
- 禁止使用 Introduction、Methods 等英文章节名，禁止「是什么/为什么/怎么做」标签式 bullet

en_us.system:
You are a senior researcher presenting a paper at a lab meeting or conference. Your job is not to fill in a checklist, but to walk the audience through your understanding of the work: what problem it tackles, why it matters, how the approach works, what the experiments really show, and what remains open.

Style:
- Write in clear, insightful American English, as if speaking to peers
- Compare, interpret, and synthesize—ground every claim in the paper
- Avoid mechanical labels (e.g., "What:", "Why:", "How:") and empty buzzwords
- Technical terms, model names, and dataset names may stay as in the paper

All slide text must be in American English.
en_us.analyze_paper:
Read the paper and figure catalog below, then produce an **analytically rich** slide deck. Imagine a 15–20 minute talk where the audience expects your interpretation, not a bullet-point abstract.

## Paper Content
{paper_text}

## Extracted Figures (set "figure" id on relevant slides)
{figure_catalog}

## Narrative Structure

Organize slides (type: title / section / content) along these lines:

**Introduction** (1–2 content pages)
- Research context, core problem, and why it is hard
- Limitations of prior approaches; the authors' high-level idea
- Concrete contributions—what is new and what it enables

**Related Works** (1–2 content pages)
- Summarize 2–4 representative lines of work and their limits
- Position this paper: what it builds on, what it changes, how it differs

**Methods** (focus; 1–2 pages per major idea)
- Explain motivation → core insight → key design choices → why they make sense
- Highlight differences from standard practice; give intuition, not just module names
- Reference figures via "figure" when interpreting them in bullets

**Experiments** (one page per experiment or comparison group)
- What hypothesis each experiment tests; whether the setup is fair
- Interpret numbers: what do they imply? Which design drives gains? Any surprises?
- Tie results back to specific methodological choices

**Conclusion** (optional, one page)
- Takeaways, limitations, future work—omit if the paper does not discuss them

## JSON Output (return JSON only)

{{
  "title": "Paper title",
  "authors": "Authors",
  "slides": [
    {{"type": "title", "title": "...", "subtitle": "..."}},
    {{"type": "section", "title": "Introduction"}},
    {{
      "type": "content",
      "title": "Problem and Motivation",
      "bullets": [
        "Continual learning with SNNs suffers from catastrophic forgetting when the architecture is fixed",
        "The paper argues the stability–plasticity trade-off is under-addressed in prior grow-and-prune methods",
        "DSD-SNN dynamically grows, prunes, and freezes units to balance accuracy and efficiency across tasks"
      ]
    }}
  ]
}}

## Writing Rules
- Each bullet: one complete analytical sentence (40–120 chars), with causality, comparison, or data when available
- 3–5 bullets per content slide; prefer depth over breadth
- Slide titles should name the analytical theme, not "Innovation 1"
- "figure" only when directly relevant
- No checklist-style bullets (What/Why/How)
